basis: Inherited hidradenitis suppurativa causes chronic autoinflammatory follicular destruction, abscesses and scarring.
Genetic essential hypertension; renal disease, stroke and other target-organ complications are separate diagnoses, not inherent involvement.
Predisposition to neuroblastoma, a sympathetic nervous system tumor; susceptibility alone does not establish adrenal dysfunction or metastatic injury.
Limb hypoplasia and cardiac malformations define the syndrome; structural tongue hypoplasia affects 80-99%.
Inherited apolipoprotein A-I deficiency disrupts HDL metabolism; premature atherosclerosis is a separate disease risk.
Dermatan-sulfate biosynthesis disorder with contractures, joint abnormalities and skin fragility; isolated PFO and blue sclerae do not establish functional damage.
Skeletal growth abnormalities and language impairment define it; strabismus occurs in 30-79%; microdontia in 2/5 supports direct dental involvement.
Immunodeficiency with autoimmunity; bronchiectasis/bullae in 1/2 establish lung damage. Crohn disease is separately diagnosed; microcytic anemia may be secondary.
Neural tumors, including schwannomas and meningiomas, are central to this predisposition; renal and other tumor sites are not universal across its subtypes.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; hearing impairment documented in 5/5 patients.
Necrotizing phlegmonous gastritis is a destructive bacterial infection of the stomach that may progress to gangrene.
Congenital skeletal dysplasia with dislocations, coalitions and spinal abnormalities; hearing impairment and developmental delay are reported in only 1-4%.
Cerebellopontine angle nerve-sheath tumor, usually vestibular schwannoma; persistent hearing loss affects roughly 80-90%.
Chronic gingival inflammation, usually driven by bacterial dental plaque; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital obstruction below the pulmonary valve affects the right ventricular outflow tract, not lung tissue.
Open spinal neural and vertebral closure defect with Chiari II; direct sacral denervation causes neurogenic bladder dysfunction in about 80-90%.
JPH2-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium; dyspnea does not establish pulmonary disease.
Hand malformations support musculoskeletal involvement; the sparse description does not establish skin dysfunction or systemic premature-aging damage.
Intellectual disability, ptosis and cleft lip define it; skeletal anomalies affect 80-99%. Hearing abnormalities and shagreen patches, also 80-99%, omitted at cap.
Benign tumor arising from male breast parenchyma; breast has no assigned axis.
Hereditary follicular atrophoderma and hypotrichosis with basal cell tumor predisposition; paraneoplastic Bazex findings and nonspecific anemia do not establish other involvement.
Inward rotation of the eyelid margin; eyelids and associated corneal injury belong to the ocular axis.
Inherited intestinal brush-border enzyme deficiency affecting carbohydrate digestion, even when sucrose intolerance is absent.
Inflammation of the facial sensory ganglion; facial weakness and taste loss reflect neuropathy. A specific infectious or autoimmune cause is not established.
Malignant tumor originates in the intima of large blood vessels; embolic or metastatic injury elsewhere is not established as common intrinsic involvement.
